# AIUC-1

AIUC-1 is a Technology, Information and Internet company. AIUC-1 Standard is a company that provides a standard for agent security, safety, and reliability. They unlock enterprise adoption and cover all risks grounded in technical testing. With over 250 security leaders, they have built a strong presence in the industry. AIUC-1 employs 115 people. Headquartered in San Francisco, United States. Its workforce is distributed across 9 countries (including United States, India, United Kingdom, Spain, and Australia).

## About

AIUC-1 is the world's first standard for AI agents. It covers data & privacy, security, safety, reliability, accountability and societal risks.

AIUC-1 was developed by the Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company in partnership with Technical Contributors from trusted institutions including Stanford, MIT, Orrick, MITRE, the Cloud Security Alliance, Google Cloud, Cisco, MongoDB, and more.

The full standard is available transparently at aiuc-1.com

  > 75% of boards have approved major AI investments, yet 48% have not set AI governance expectations, according to Grant Thornton's 2026 AI Impact survey.
  >
  > AI risk is ultimately the board's duty to oversee. In our latest whitepaper, Louise McElvogue, along with AIUC-1 Consortium members and directors sitting on boards across healthcare, financial services and other critical industries set out the 3 immediate priorities boards must follow to better govern AI risk:
  >
  > 1. Operationalize AI principles: turn values into measurable controls
  > 2. Build AI fluency: foster collective AI fluency so that the board can appropriately challenge what they are governing
  > 3. Own AI governance: set decision boundaries upfront, rather than reviewing agent decisions after the fact
  >
  > Thank you to Louise McElvogue and all contributors for shaping this whitepaper.

- [2026-09-24 · Posted · 148 reactions] [MSCI Inc. expects to run more than a thousand AI agents across the...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aiuc-1_msci-inc-expects-to-run-more-than-a-thousand-activity-7508911771894837248-p5vP)
  > MSCI Inc. expects to run more than a thousand AI agents across the company within 18 months. Its indexes benchmark trillions of dollars and its controls are supervised by regulators in the US, UK and EU.
  >
  > MSCI needs assurance that an agent behaves under adversarial pressure, or produces evidence an auditor can rely on.
  >
  > In John R.' words, CISO of MSCI:
  > "We had an AI governance program, we were working on ISO 42001 and we had SOC 2 with an independent auditor. None of it answered the question I knew our auditors would ask. Not 'do you have a policy?' but 'does this agent actually do what the policy says, and can you prove it?'"
  >
  > MSCI is now using AIUC-1 to manage agentic security at scale:
  > 1. Every agent is tiered based on its risk profile
  > 2. Agents in the highest risk tier are certified against AIUC-1 with an independent auditor
  > 3. Lower-tier agents comply with a defined subset of AIUC-1 requirements at build time through a shift-left approach
  >
  > MSCI's SecOps Agent, which approves requests for privileged Azure roles, was the first to go through the process end to end. It is in scope for MSCI's external SOX audit. AIUC ran ~1,400 evals across 112 privileged roles, drawing on adversarial techniques including authority impersonation, prompt injection and jailbreaks.
  >
  > The agent passed with no major or significant vulnerabilities, and the signed attestation and report have been submitted to MSCI's auditors for their 2026 SOX audit.
  >
  > Congratulations to John and the MSCI team on this milestone.
  >
  > Read the full case study: https://lnkd.in/g9RxBdkz

- [2026-09-23 · Posted · 103 reactions] [Collibra holds the metadata, policies, lineage and access rules...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aiuc-1_collibra-holds-the-metadata-policies-lineage-activity-7508562126123208705-_sLc)
  > Collibra holds the metadata, policies, lineage and access rules that describe an organization's most sensitive assets. Today, they announce their AIUC-1 certification.
  >
  > The certification covers Maestro Assistant, the conversational assistant built into the Collibra Platform that lets users ask questions about their data, policies, lineage and AI systems and receive answers grounded in governed context.
  >
  > To earn the certification, Collibra:
  > 1. Submitted the agent to comprehensive technical testing across data leakage, hallucinations, and unsafe tool calls
  > 2. Demonstrated that all applicable AIUC-1 requirements were met across legal policies, operational practices and technical controls
  > 3. Passed an independent audit by Schellman
  >
  > Congrats to the entire Collibra team on this milestone!

- [2026-09-22 · Posted · 33 reactions] [Phil Venables has spent 30 years as the CISO of Goldman Sachs and...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aiuc-1_phil-venables-has-spent-30-years-as-the-ciso-activity-7508260684732710912-of3D)

properties.description:
AIUC-1 is the world's first standard for AI agents. It covers data & privacy, security, safety, reliability, accountability and societal risks.

AIUC-1 was developed by the Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company in partnership with Technical Contributors from trusted institutions including Stanford, MIT, Orrick, MITRE, the Cloud Security Alliance, Google Cloud, Cisco, MongoDB, and more.

The full standard is available transparently at aiuc-1.com
